name: Same-platform rebalancing arbitrage: YES+NO sets and NegRisk converter / baskets
maturity: Established but effectively closed to newcomers (verify)
one_line: Lock the complement identity in one binary (merge/split) and the NO-to-YES conversion identity in neg-risk events; large historically, saturated and fee-gated now.
scope: Cover single-condition long/short set arbitrage and neg-risk rebalancing: mechanics of split, merge, convert, redeem via the gasless relayer and V2 adapter; reconcile the ~$40M headline ($10.58M single-condition + $29.02M neg-risk) with the execution-aware $1.12M reconstruction (97% converter-enabled, 81% from partial conversions and inventory recycling, top-10 = 75%, median profit per conversion $0.08, violations lasting seconds). Explain YES-side residual as capital-lockup carry, augmented neg-risk 'Other' pitfalls, per-leg taker fees since 2026-03-30, fee-free geopolitics and maker-legged variants, orphan-leg evidence (60/69 pairs). Boundary: logical dependencies across separate markets go to combinatorial-logical-arbitrage; crypto split-sell as a maker business is short-crypto-maker-side; reverted-fill counterparties are ghost-fills-bot-hunting.

critic_notes: rebalancing-arbitrage-yesno-negrisk: 'Established' should read 'established and effectively closed': median $0.08 per conversion, ten addresses hold 75%, violations last seconds, per-leg fees since 2026-03-30. The residual YES-basket side is capital-lock carry, not arbitrage.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: NegRisk converter / basket arbitrage (smaller than people think)
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Use the NegRisk adapter's NO->YES-basket conversion and YES+NO / multi-outcome sums to lock riskless spreads.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: In negative-risk events, a NO share in one outcome converts into YES shares of all others, so baskets whose executable cost is below payoff can be formed and recycled before settlement. A depth-aware reconstruction finds ~$1.12M total executable arbitrage profit, $1.086M of it via the converter and only ~$32k via settlement-based baskets; violations cluster on the YES side where no converter exists. In NBA markets, 290 combinatorial episodes yielded a median 101 bps. Community wallet-watching shows accounts buying YES and NO for ~1c/share locks with huge capital tie-up.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Protocol primitives most traders do not use; speed.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: It mostly does not for newcomers: totals are small relative to platform volume and dominated by incumbents.
raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Leg risk (a simple 0.48/0.48 BTC up/down bot completed 60 of 69 pairs and the 9 orphans ate all profit), fees on all categories since 2026-03-30 (one Reddit title: 'arbitrage strategies are done'), capital lock until resolution when no converter path exists, gas/relayer limits.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Scan read-only for a week: count executable (depth-aware, fee-aware) violations >50 bps and their lifetime; compare with your order round-trip time.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: NegRisk converter arbitrage including partial conversions and inventory recycling
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Buy NO baskets (or subsets) in mutually-exclusive events and convert through the NegRisk adapter to collateral + YES, recycling inventory; the only same-platform arbitrage channel with material realised profit, now heavily competed.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: In an n-outcome negRisk event, holding NO on k outcomes converts to (k-1) units of collateral plus YES on the complement. Bots accumulate NO legs, largely with maker-assisted fills (~80%), convert, and sell or hold the resulting YES. 81% of realised profit came from partial conversions and inventory recycling rather than clean full-set conversions. The plain alternative - buying every YES (or every NO) and holding the basket to settlement - earned only $32k in the whole sample.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Transient incoherence of multi-outcome books (sum of prices != 1) plus the adapter's ability to release collateral early; YES-side violations are ~58x more frequent than NO-side on the CLOB (2,098 vs 36 episodes).
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: It probably does not any more for a new entrant: top-10 addresses take 75% and median profit per conversion is $0.08; the residual edge is in maker-assisted leg accumulation and inventory recycling, not detection speed.

evidence.title: Executable Arbitrage and Market Efficiency in Prediction Markets (Gebele, Mutzel, Matthes), arXiv
evidence.supports: 259M trades through 2025-12-31: $1.12M total executable arbitrage profit; $1.086M converter-enabled (core full-set conversions $205,531 = 18.9%, partial/recycling $880,469 = 81.1%); settlement-based baskets $32,283 (5,923 CLOB baskets); top-10 addresses 75%; median profit per conversion $1 -> $0.20 -> $0.08; exact-duration violations median 16.15 s (YES) / 7.99 s (NO); one excluded 7-minute anomaly on 2025-12-12 produced $381,748 from 75 conversions.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Single-condition YES+NO rebalancing (buy both under $1 / split and sell both over $1)
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Lock the complement identity inside one binary market via merge or split.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Long side: when best ask YES + best ask NO < $1, buy both and merge the set into $1 collateral. Short side: when bids sum > $1, split $1 into a set and sell both legs. Both are atomic in payoff terms but not in execution, so legging risk exists. Typical realized margins were 1-5%.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Transient book dislocations during news/volatility; retail market orders sweeping one side.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: It paid $10.6M in a year pre-fees, but the per-opportunity window has collapsed to seconds in liquid markets; remaining value is in the long tail of thin markets and in volatile moments.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Taker fees on both legs since March 2026 (up to 2x fee at mid prices); one-leg fills; ghost-fill style counterparties historically cancelled the matched leg; windows of seconds need co-located infra.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: NegRisk basket rebalancing and NO->YES conversion arbitrage
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Exploit multi-outcome events where the YES prices do not sum to 1, using the NegRisk adapter's convert path.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: In negative-risk events one NO token converts atomically into one YES of every other outcome. When NO prices are cheap relative to the basket, bots buy NO, convert, and sell or hold the resulting YES set; when all YES sum below $1 they buy the basket and wait for settlement. Only the NO->YES direction is executable before settlement, so NO-side violations are short-lived while YES-side violations persist and require capital lock-up to resolution. Augmented events add placeholder/'Other' outcomes that must not be traded.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Protocol asymmetry: one direction is an executable primitive, the other is a carry trade; many-leg books drift as retail piles into one candidate.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: This was by far the largest realized arbitrage pool ($29M in a year). The residual is a financing business on the YES side that HFT bots avoid because capital is tied up.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Multi-leg execution with taker fees per leg; depth on the cheapest legs is tiny; augmented NegRisk 'Other' redefinitions; capital locked for months on YES-basket carry; adapter migration (V2) broke old integrations.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Neg-risk convert / split / merge arbitrage under the 2026 fee regime
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Event-level arbitrage through the NegRisk adapter and full-set split/merge still exists but must now be run maker-legged or in fee-free categories, with gasless relayer operations.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: In neg-risk events 1 NO of any outcome converts atomically into 1 YES of every other outcome (releasing collateral when several NOs are converted), and any binary market allows split of 1 pUSD into YES+NO and merge back. When the sum of YES asks across an event is below 1, or the sum of NO asks is below n-1, buying the set and converting/merging/redeeming locks a profit. A peer-reviewed-style on-chain study estimated about $40M of realised arbitrage profit on Polymarket from exactly these single-market and cross-market inconsistencies. Since Fee Structure V2 each taker leg costs feeRate x p x (1-p) per share (up to 1.0-1.75c), so an n-leg taker arb needs a gap of several cents; the surviving variants are (a) geopolitics and other zero-fee markets where conversion arb is still frictionless, (b) maker-legged arbs that rest the legs and collect rebates, (c) augmented neg-risk events where converted NO sets also deliver the unnamed placeholder and Other outcomes. Split, merge, convert and redeem are gas-free through the builder relayer; the v1 adapter was retired 2026-07-17.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Mechanical no-arbitrage identities enforced only by traders; fees and leg risk now deter most bots, leaving wider but rarer gaps.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Fee-aware routing (which legs to take, which to rest, which category) is a second-order optimisation most legacy arb bots written for the zero-fee era do not do.
raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Leg risk when resting; 1 s / 50 ms matching delays on some markets; adapter convert fee parameter exists in the contract design (current value unverified); Other/placeholder semantics in augmented events can change payoff assumptions; competition from the same bots that took the $40M.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Replay one month of book snapshots for all neg-risk events, compute set-arb gaps net of per-market feeSchedule, and split results by fee-free vs fee-enabled category and by taker vs maker-legged execution.
